QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_15

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF) has a target corpus of INR 400 crore. It expects to onboard investors at the minimum ticket size. Ignoring AIF employees and Accredited Investors, what is the MAXIMUM number of external investors that could fully subscribe the corpus, and which regulatory cap binds first?

answer.text: 400 investors; the minimum ticket (INR 1 crore x 400 = INR 400 crore) binds first
1,000 investors; the 1,000-investor cap binds first since INR 1 crore x 1,000 = INR 1,000 crore exceeds corpus
2,000 investors; the 2,000 Companies Act private placement cap binds
200 investors; the Angel Fund 200-investor cap applies

explanation.text: The Logic: At the INR 1 crore minimum ticket for Cat III AIFs, fully subscribing an INR 400 crore corpus requires at most 400 investors. The 1,000-investor cap is not binding at this corpus size, so the minimum-ticket arithmetic binds first. The Trap: Option B gets the cap right but misidentifies which constraint binds first at this corpus. Option C cites a Companies Act number that is not the AIF investor cap. Option D applies an Angel Fund (Cat I sub-category) rule that does not apply to a Cat III fund. Note: The workbook supports the INR 1 crore minimum Category III AIF ticket, the INR 20 crore minimum corpus, employee/accredited-investor carve-outs, and the 1,000-investor maximum.
